# Muni Yields Are Attractive


The war in Iran has increased volatility across fixed income markets, pushing municipal bond yields higher as investors reassess inflation risk, energy costs and the path of Federal Reserve policy. Even so, historically elevated municipal bond yields present a compelling opportunity for tax-sensitive investors.


Enlarge


The war in Iran has added pressure to fixed income markets, particularly in U.S. Treasuries. The 10-year Treasury yield recently traded near 4.7% as investors repriced inflation risk and the economic effects of higher energy costs, and what that may mean for monetary policy. At the same time, municipal bond yields have risen as well, with 10-year tax-free bond yields reaching roughly 3.8% or 6.3% on a tax-equivalent basis. This is key because entry-point yield is often a strong indicator of long-term return potential.


While yield volatility is likely to persist, our Tax-Managed Fixed Income solution seeks to uncover value in the municipal bond market through disciplined security selection, active risk management and tax-aware portfolio management.

[Play the Long Game](https://www.bny.com/wealth/global/en/insights/chart-of-the-week/play-the-long-game.html)


When it comes to investing, time matters. While headlines and short-term perspectives can lead investors to try to time the market, investors have historically been rewarded by playing the long game. Rather than overreacting to market noise, investing over longer time periods can help smooth the ride without sacrificing returns. The lesson: stay diversified and invested for the long term.


Article | Chart of the Week


[Contained Contagion?](https://www.bny.com/wealth/global/en/insights/chart-of-the-week/contained-contagion.html)


U.S. high yield credit spreads have widened year to date, reflecting greater investor caution about perceived default risk. The move also raises concerns about possible credit contagion. However, because spread widening has been concentrated in the lowest-quality issuers rather than higher-quality issuers, we don’t anticipate broader market stress.


Article | Chart of the Week


[Can the Bull Run in Corporate Margins Continue?](https://www.bny.com/wealth/global/en/insights/chart-of-the-week/can-the-bull-run-in-corporate-margins-continue.html)


Higher inflation and elevated interest rates typically weigh on corporate profitability, yet corporate margins continue to climb to record highs. While that strength is evident both in the U.S. and abroad, U.S. outperformance versus Europe is now the widest on record. Stronger margins have helped contribute to better-than-expected earnings and reinforce U.S. equity leadership. The question now is whether that strength can persist.

[Higher Rates, but Lower Sensitivity](https://www.bny.com/wealth/global/en/insights/chart-of-the-week/higher-rates-but-lower-sensitivity.html)


Higher interest rates have become a frequently cited risk to corporate earnings and the economy. The conventional thinking is straightforward: when borrowing costs rise, companies face higher interest expenses, profits come under pressure, and economic growth slows. While there is truth to that relationship, the current cycle may differ from investors’ expectations.
